title: Steak Frites
subtitle: French bistro steak and chips
excerpt: A well-seared bavette or sirloin steak with a quick shallot and red wine butter sauce and proper twice-cooked chips. The French bistro pairing.
steak: A well-seared bavette or sirloin steak with proper twice-cooked chips. This is the French bistro dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Steak frites is the definitive dish of the Parisian brasserie and bistro, closely associated with the working-class restaurants of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The dish appears in countless French cookbooks and is one of the most ordered dishes in Paris.

recipeTools.notes: For the steak. Gets very hot and holds it.
Or a large deep saucepan for the chips.

content.text: Steak frites is a well-seared steak and twice-cooked chips. The chips are blanched in oil at a low temperature, drained, then fried again at high heat just before serving, which gives a crisp exterior and a fluffy interior. The steak sauce is made from the pan juices with shallot, red wine, and butter.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into 1 cm thick chips

content.text: For the chips: heat the oil to 130 C. Fry the chips in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until cooked through but not coloured. Drain on a wire rack and leave to cool. They can sit for up to 2 hours at this stage.
When ready to serve, heat the oil to 190 C. Fry the chips again for 3 to 4 minutes until very crisp and golden. Drain and season with salt immediately.
For the steak: season generously on both sides with salt and pepper at least 30 minutes before cooking. Heat a cast-iron skillet over a very high heat until smoking. Add the oil.

Cook the steak for 2 to 3 minutes per side for medium-rare, pressing it down so it makes full contact with the pan. In the last minute, add the butter and thyme and baste the steak. Rest on a warm plate for at least 5 minutes.

In the same pan, cook the shallot over a medium heat for 2 minutes. Add the red wine and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Swirl in the remaining butter. Season and pour over the rested steak.
